subject: Onboarding: model fit decisions and throughput bins
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@clearpath.ai>, Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-14T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding: model fit decisions and throughput bins

Hi Jordan / Emma —

As we kick off the implementation handoff, attached is a short worksheet (clearpath_model_decision_workbook.xlsx) with the model shortlist, tradeoffs, and an empty throughput bin chart we use to lock sizing. Quick summary below to make it easier for your team to respond:

Model shortlist (recommended variants):
- Mosaic-7B / 4-bit quantized (cost-optimized, good for conversational summarization)
- Llama2-13B / Q8 (balanced accuracy + latency)
- Falcon-40B-Chat / Q8 (higher quality for long-form generation, higher cost)

Key decisions we need from ClearPath this week:
1) Preferred model tier (cost-first vs quality-first). If you can rank the three that helps us pick fallback rules.
2) Context window requirement: do you need 4k, 8k, or 16k effective context for the primary flows? If some flows need longer context, list which ones.
3) Estimated request profile for month 1 (we included a short sample table in the workbook):
   - expected DAU (approx)
   - average tokens per request (prompt + generated), and percent of requests that are >2k tokens
   - expected traffic spikes (e.g., peak RPS/hour) and whether predictable (batch runs) or bursty

Why this matters: these answers determine the preferred serving configuration (single-shard low-latency vs batched throughput), KV cache strategy, and which quantized model variant we recommend.

Proposed internal plan after we get your answers:
- We map the workbook numbers to hourly token bands and recommend a starting Dedicated config + safe autoscale thresholds.
- We run a short synthetic spike sim against the shortlisted variants and share latency vs cost tradeoffs.
- Implementation kickoff call to lock the rollout date and canary slicing.

Attachments: model-shortlist-brief.pdf, clearpath_model_decision_workbook.xlsx

Can you reply with the three decision items above by EOD Friday? If you want, we can take a quick 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the workbook.

Thanks —
Tessa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@clearpath.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearpath.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model fit decisions and throughput bins

Tessa — thanks for the clear worksheet. Emma and I reviewed with engineering; answers below and we've attached sample_payloads_and_annotations.jsonl with 50 representative requests.

1) Model preference: Mosaic-7B (quantized) as primary for MVP. If that shows quality regressions on the summarization task we will fallback to Llama2-13B. Falcon-40B is out for MVP due to cost.

2) Context window: primary flows (real-time summarization from meeting transcripts) need ~8k effective context for acceptable chunk consolidation. Long-form batch summarization (nightly jobs) can use 16k if available, but initially can be batched and run on a higher-memory queue.

3) Request profile (Month 1 expected):
   - DAU: 2,500 active users (concurrent peak ~350 users during 9am-11am PT)
   - Avg tokens/request: 1,200 (prompt 600 + generation 600)
   - Percent >2k tokens: ~8% (mostly long transcripts)
   - Typical peak: sustained peak RPS converting to ~75 requests/minute across the service; occasional bursts up to 180 req/min during product release days

Estimated monthly token volume (back-of-envelope): 2,500 DAU * 15 requests/user/month * 1,200 tokens/request = ~45,000,000 tokens/month. Expect +20% headroom for growth in month 1.

Notes:
- Low tolerance for high tail latency in the real-time flow (SLO target: p95 < 450ms for the conversational summarization endpoint).
- For batch summarization we prefer throughput over latency.

We'll plan a call Friday at 11:00am PT to walk the sample payloads if that works for you.

— Jordan
Director of Product
ClearPath Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@clearpath.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-15T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: model fit decisions and throughput bins

Thanks Jordan — this is super helpful and the sample payloads look representative. A few follow-ups so implementation can size and propose a configuration: 

- Based on 45M tokens/mo and wanting p95 < 450ms for the real-time endpoint, our preliminary recommendation is: Mosaic-7B quantized on dedicated 4-GPU pool with continuous batching disabled for the low-latency path and an autoscale buffer that buys +25% headroom. This keeps latency low for the 9–11am peak while still minimizing cost.

- For the 8k context requirement: we'll provision a separate higher-memory node type for the long-context batch path. We'll use streaming sharding for live summarization and a batched worker pool for nightly jobs.

- Fallbacks: Llama2-13B (Q8) as a warm fallback route for requests flagged for higher-quality when Mosaic scores low on our eval harness. Redwood can automatically route to fallback for a configurable percent of traffic during rollout.

Action items for us before Friday call:
1) I'll drop an initial Dedicated sizing proposal into the shared Drive folder with estimated monthly cost bands (low/expected/high).
2) Monica, can you draft the canary slices for the first 2 weeks (percent rollout, health checks we should run)?
3) Tessa will coordinate the Friday call with ClearPath to confirm the rollout date and acceptance criteria.

On quoting Jordan's earlier point: can you confirm whether the 20% headroom is acceptable for sizing (we can also propose an aggressive autoscale policy instead)?

Ben
Senior Product Manager, Inference
Redwood Inference

If all good we will schedule the implementation sprint for the week of 6/26 and start canary on 7/03. Please reply if you need the kickoff pushed.

Thanks —
Tessa
